title: The Standing of a Certificate of Deposit Once Its Grace Period Has Run
content:
Where no grace action has closed the certificate, its standing on the day after the grace period ends follows the renewal instruction recorded against it.

## 1. The two dispositions

**Under an instruction to renew automatically.** The certificate runs again in the tier its own renewal target names, or in the tier the owner chose during grace, and the new term starts on the maturity date of the term that ended. An instruction to renew automatically is honoured only on a tier that offers automatic renewal.

**Under an instruction to pay out.** The whole balance is paid out as a maturity payout, to the payout account recorded against the certificate or by an official check, and the certificate closes.

## 2. The new term begins at maturity, not at the end of grace

The new term's first day is the maturity date of the term that ended, although the disposition itself is settled on the day after grace ends. The grace days therefore fall inside the new term, not between the two terms.

## 3. After grace has run

Once the grace period has ended, money taken out of the certificate is again a withdrawal before maturity, judged against the term now running rather than the term that ended. The freedom the grace days gave is not carried forward.

## 4. Points of judgement

| Standing at the end of grace | Disposition |
|---|---|
| balance still standing, instruction to renew automatically, tier offers it | runs again from the maturity date, in the target tier or the tier chosen during grace |
| balance still standing, instruction to pay out | whole balance paid to the payout account or by official check, certificate closed |
| balance already withdrawn in full during grace | the certificate was closed by that grace action, and nothing falls to be done |

A certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line that matured on 4 March and whose grace period runs 10 days takes its disposition on 15 March, and where it renews, the new term is dated from 4 March.
